newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Novopharm sees 30-35 pct Zantac discount.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Novopharm sees 30-35 pct Zantac discount.

text.p: Canadian generic drug maker Novopharm Ltd said on Monday it expected to undercut Glaxo Wellcome Plc 's ulcer drug Zantac by between 30 and 35 percent in the first few weeks of sale.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chairman and chief executive officer Leslie Dan also said he hoped to achieve sale of "$150 to $175 million at least" in the first 30 days that the drug was on sale.

Dan also said his new found ally Genpharm, owned by Germany's Merck KGgA, had indicated it could be possible to extend the period under which Novopharm can sell the drug exclusively in the U.S. by four to six weeks beyond the current August 29 limit.

Dan said the company's sales of Ranitidine Hydrochloride should be profitable enough to cover the costs of a wasted $70 million payment made to Glaxo Wellcome before Novopharm's right to sell the drug from July 10 was stopped by legal action.
It would also cover an undisclosed profit-sharing arrangement with Genpharm, he said.
"We were in a difficult position where we had the product and Genpharm had the exclusive licence but no product because they were in litigation with Glaxo Wellcome," Dan said.
Dan said the agreement with Genpharm would last until December 31, after which Genpharm would start marketing its own version of Zantac, which had sales of around $1.6 billion in the U.S. last year.
"Genpharm believe they can further extend exclusivity beyond August 29," said Dan, after which he said the only competition might be from Novartis AG's U.S. unit Geneva Pharmaceuticals Inc.
Dan said the way generic drugs were admitted to the U.S. market needed to be overhauled.
"I think the entire generic industry would like to have some clarification. You have got an 'Alice in Wonderland' situation right now," he added.
